1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Local CSV cleaner: apply one explicit rule to one column of a UTF-8 CSV.
3	
4	Usage:
5	    python csv_cleaner.py --input input.csv --output cleaned.csv \
6	        --column name --rule trim
7	
8	normalize-null additionally accepts repeatable custom null markers:
9	
10	    python csv_cleaner.py --input input.csv --output cleaned.csv \
11	        --column name --rule normalize-null \
12	        --null-marker MISSING --null-marker 待补
13	
14	normalize-null also accepts --null-replacement TEXT to substitute the
15	given text for every cell the rule would otherwise turn into an empty
16	string:
17	
18	    python csv_cleaner.py --input input.csv --output cleaned.csv \
19	        --column name --rule normalize-null --null-replacement 未知
20	
21	The replacement is written verbatim: it is not stripped, not
22	case-folded and never re-matched against the null markers, and an
23	empty or whitespace-only replacement is allowed. Omitting the option
24	keeps the default empty-string behavior. Cells whose value does not
25	match a marker are kept byte-for-byte either way, and a cell only
26	counts as changed when the replacement differs from its original
27	value.
28	
29	The field delimiter is chosen explicitly with --delimiter:
30	
31	    python csv_cleaner.py --input sample.csv --output cleaned.csv \
32	        --column name --rule trim --delimiter semicolon
33	
34	    --delimiter accepts only the lowercase names comma, semicolon and
35	    tab, meaning a comma, a semicolon and one real tab character
36	    respectively; omitting it is the same as comma. The chosen
37	    delimiter is used both to read the input and to write the result,
38	    never guessed from the file contents.
39	
40	    The export delimiter can be chosen independently with
41	    --output-delimiter:
42	
43	    python csv_cleaner.py --input sample.csv --output cleaned.csv \
44	        --column name --rule trim --delimiter semicolon \
45	        --output-delimiter comma
46	
47	    --output-delimiter accepts the same lowercase names comma,
48	    semicolon and tab. When given it overrides only the output format:
49	    the input is still read with --delimiter, and any of the three
50	    combinations is allowed. Omitting it keeps one shared delimiter for
51	    reading and writing (comma when --delimiter is also omitted). A
52	    change of delimiter is only a format change and never counts as a
53	    changed cell.
54	
55	normalize-date additionally accepts --date-order to choose how a slash
56	date with the year last is read:
57	
58	    python csv_cleaner.py --input input.csv --output cleaned.csv \
59	        --column due_date --rule normalize-date --date-order mdy
60	
61	    --date-order accepts only lowercase dmy and mdy; omitting it is the
62	    same as dmy (DD/MM/YYYY). Under mdy the year-last slash date is read
63	    as MM/DD/YYYY, with ambiguous fields settled by the chosen order and
64	    no guessing or fallback. YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY/MM/DD and YYYY.MM.DD stay
65	    year-month-day under either order.
66	
67	normalize-whitespace strips both ends and collapses every internal run
68	of whitespace (judged by str.isspace) to one ASCII space:
69	
70	    python csv_cleaner.py --input input.csv --output cleaned.csv \
71	        --column name --rule normalize-whitespace
72	
73	On success prints a single JSON object to stdout, e.g.
74	    {"rows": 3, "changed_cells": 2}
75	and exits 0. Any failure exits 2 with the reason on stderr and no output
76	file is created.
77	
78	With --include-changes the same JSON object gains a "changes" array with
79	one {"record", "column", "before", "after"} entry per changed cell, in
80	record order; no separate detail file is written.
81	
82	With --include-null-matches (normalize-null only) the summary also gains
83	a "null_matches" array with one {"record", "column", "before"} entry per
84	cell the null rule matches, in record order, whether or not the
85	replacement actually changes the cell text; the exported CSV is
86	unaffected and no separate detail file is written. The two detail
87	switches are independent and may be used together.
88	
89	With --dry-run the input is fully read and validated and the same summary
90	JSON is printed, but no output file or directory is created. The output
91	path must still differ from the input and must not already exist; a
92	missing parent directory or unwritable location does not fail the
93	preview, so a successful dry run does not guarantee a real export would
94	succeed.
95	"""
96	
97	import argparse
98	import csv
99	import json
100	import os
101	import re
102	import sys
103	from datetime import date
104	from functools import partial
105	
106	NULL_MARKERS = frozenset({"null", "n/a"})
107	
108	# [0-9] rather than \d so only ASCII digits are accepted.
109	DATE_ISO_RE = re.compile(r"^([0-9]{4})-([0-9]{2})-([0-9]{2})$")
110	# A slash date whose four-digit year is last. The two leading fields are
111	# day/month under dmy and month/day under mdy, never guessed.
112	DATE_SLASH_YEAR_RE = re.compile(r"^([0-9]{2})/([0-9]{2})/([0-9]{4})$")
113	DATE_YMD_SLASH_RE = re.compile(r"^([0-9]{4})/([0-9]{2})/([0-9]{2})$")
114	# A dot date is always year-month-day; the two English periods are part
115	# of the spelling and --date-order never applies to it.
116	DATE_DOT_RE = re.compile(r"^([0-9]{4})\.([0-9]{2})\.([0-9]{2})$")
117	
118	# Accepted --date-order values: how to read a NN/NN/YYYY slash date.
119	DATE_ORDERS = ("dmy", "mdy")
120	DEFAULT_DATE_ORDER = "dmy"
121	
122	# Accepted --delimiter / --output-delimiter names mapped to the actual
123	# one-character field delimiters. Each is always explicit: the input
124	# delimiter defaults to comma, and the output delimiter defaults to the
125	# input one; neither is ever sniffed.
126	DELIMITERS = {"comma": ",", "semicolon": ";", "tab": "\t"}
127	DEFAULT_DELIMITER_NAME = "comma"
128	
129	
130	class InvalidDateError(ValueError):
131	    """Raised when a cell is not an accepted calendar date."""
132	
133	
134	def ascii_lower(text):
135	    """Lowercase ASCII A-Z only; all other characters stay untouched."""
136	    return "".join(
137	        chr(ord(ch) + 32) if "A" <= ch <= "Z" else ch for ch in text
138	    )
139	
140	
141	def is_null_match(value, extra_markers=frozenset()):
142	    """Return True when the null rule would replace the cell.
143	
144	    After stripping both ends, the cell matches when the result is empty
145	    or equals NULL / N/A (or any of the given extra markers)
146	    case-insensitively with respect to ASCII letters. Anything else
147	    (e.g. "NULLABLE") does not match.
148	    """
149	    stripped = value.strip()
150	    if not stripped:
151	        return True
152	    lowered = ascii_lower(stripped)
153	    return lowered in NULL_MARKERS or lowered in extra_markers
154	
155	
156	def normalize_null(value, extra_markers=frozenset(), replacement=""):
157	    """Normalize null markers to the replacement text (empty by default).
158	
159	    After stripping both ends, the cell is replaced when the result is
160	    empty or matches NULL / N/A (or any of the given extra markers)
161	    case-insensitively with respect to ASCII letters. Anything else is
162	    returned byte-for-byte, including its surrounding whitespace (e.g.
163	    "NULLABLE" is not a marker). Extra markers are compared after
164	    str.strip() themselves; duplicate markers collapse into one match but
165	    never inflate the change count. The replacement is used verbatim: it
166	    is not stripped, not case-folded and never re-matched against the
167	    markers, and an empty or whitespace-only replacement is allowed.
168	    """
169	    if is_null_match(value, extra_markers):
170	        return replacement
171	    return value
172	
173	
174	# Accepted spellings that are always read year-month-day; the separator
175	# is part of the spelling and the three are never mixed within a value.
176	DATE_YMD_PATTERNS = (DATE_ISO_RE, DATE_YMD_SLASH_RE, DATE_DOT_RE)
177	
178	
179	def parse_date_fields(stripped, date_order):
180	    """Split an accepted date spelling into (year, month, day) ints.
181	
182	    The three YYYY-first spellings always read year-month-day regardless
183	    of date_order. The year-last slash spelling NN/NN/YYYY follows the
184	    explicit order only: "dmy" reads it DD/MM/YYYY and "mdy" reads it
185	    MM/DD/YYYY, with no guessing or fallback. Returns None when stripped
186	    matches none of the accepted spellings.
187	    """
188	    for pattern in DATE_YMD_PATTERNS:
189	        match = pattern.match(stripped)
190	        if match:
191	            return tuple(int(part) for part in match.groups())
192	    match = DATE_SLASH_YEAR_RE.match(stripped)
193	    if match:
194	        first, second, year = (int(part) for part in match.groups())
195	        if date_order == "mdy":
196	            return year, first, second
197	        return year, second, first
198	    return None
199	
200	
201	def normalize_date(value, date_order=DEFAULT_DATE_ORDER):
202	    """Normalize an accepted date spelling to YYYY-MM-DD.
203	
204	    After stripping both ends, an empty cell stays empty. Anything else
205	    must be exactly YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY/MM/DD, YYYY.MM.DD or a slash date
206	    with the four-digit year last (NN/NN/YYYY), using ASCII digits, a
207	    four-digit year and two-digit month/day, and must be a real
208	    proleptic Gregorian calendar date in years 0001-9999; the result is
209	    always spelled YYYY-MM-DD.
210	
211	    YYYY.MM.DD is always read year-month-day with two English periods;
212	    like YYYY-MM-DD and YYYY/MM/DD it is unaffected by date_order. The
213	    year-last slash date is read by the explicit date_order only:
214	    "dmy" reads it as DD/MM/YYYY and "mdy" as MM/DD/YYYY. Ambiguous
215	    values follow that order with no guessing or fallback (under mdy
216	    13/02/2024 means month 13 and is invalid). YYYY-MM-DD,
217	    YYYY/MM/DD and YYYY.MM.DD are always year-month-day under either
218	    order. Internal whitespace, unpadded numbers, mixed separators,
219	    time suffixes and null markers such as NULL or N/A are invalid and
220	    raise InvalidDateError.
221	    """
222	    stripped = value.strip()
223	    if not stripped:
224	        return ""
225	    fields = parse_date_fields(stripped, date_order)
226	    if fields is None:
227	        raise InvalidDateError(f"invalid date: {value!r}")
228	    year, month, day = fields
229	    try:
230	        normalized = date(year, month, day)
231	    except ValueError:
232	        raise InvalidDateError(f"invalid date: {value!r}") from None
233	    return normalized.isoformat()
234	
235	
236	def normalize_whitespace(value):
237	    """Collapse whitespace to single ASCII spaces and strip both ends.
238	
239	    Whitespace is judged by str.isspace (space, tab, carriage return,
240	    newline, ideographic space U+3000, ...): both ends are stripped and
241	    every internal run of whitespace becomes one ASCII space. An empty
242	    string stays empty and a whitespace-only string becomes empty. All
243	    other characters and their order are preserved, including the
244	    zero-width space U+200B, which str.isspace does not count as
245	    whitespace. NULL / N/A text and date text are only
246	    whitespace-normalized, never otherwise converted.
247	    """
248	    return " ".join(value.split())
249	
250	
251	RULES = {
252	    "trim": str.strip,
253	    "normalize-null": normalize_null,
254	    "normalize-date": normalize_date,
255	    "normalize-whitespace": normalize_whitespace,
256	}
257	
258	
259	def fail(message):
260	    print(f"error: {message}", file=sys.stderr)
261	    sys.exit(2)
262	
263	
264	def parse_args(argv):
265	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
266	        prog="csv_cleaner.py",
267	        description="Apply one explicit cleaning rule to one column of a "
268	                    "UTF-8 CSV file and write the result to a new file.",
269	    )
270	    parser.add_argument("--input", required=True,
271	                        help="path to the input CSV file (opened read-only)")
272	    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True,
273	                        help="path to the output CSV file (must not exist yet)")
274	    parser.add_argument("--column", required=True,
275	                        help="exact name of the single column to clean")
276	    parser.add_argument("--rule", required=True,
277	                        help="cleaning rule to apply (supported: "
278	                             + ", ".join(sorted(RULES)) + ")")
279	    parser.add_argument("--null-marker", action="append", default=[],
280	                        metavar="MARKER",
281	                        help="additional whole-value null marker for "
282	                             "normalize-null (may be repeated; the value "
283	                             "is stripped at both ends and compared "
284	                             "case-insensitively on ASCII letters only)")
285	    parser.add_argument("--null-replacement", default=None,
286	                        metavar="TEXT",
287	                        help="replacement text for normalize-null: every "
288	                             "cell the rule would turn into an empty "
289	                             "string is written as TEXT instead, verbatim "
290	                             "(not stripped, not case-folded, never "
291	                             "re-matched; empty and whitespace-only text "
292	                             "is allowed); omitting it keeps the default "
293	                             "empty-string behavior")
294	    parser.add_argument("--date-order", choices=DATE_ORDERS, default=None,
295	                        metavar="ORDER",
296	                        help="how to read a slash date with the year last "
297	                             "for normalize-date: dmy (DD/MM/YYYY, the "
298	                             "default when omitted) or mdy (MM/DD/YYYY); "
299	                             "YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY/MM/DD and YYYY.MM.DD stay "
300	                             "year-month-day under either order")
301	    parser.add_argument("--delimiter", choices=sorted(DELIMITERS),
302	                        default=DEFAULT_DELIMITER_NAME,
303	                        metavar="NAME",
304	                        help="field delimiter for reading the input "
305	                             "(and for writing unless --output-delimiter "
306	                             "is given): comma (the default when "
307	                             "omitted), semicolon or tab (one real tab "
308	                             "character); the delimiter is never guessed "
309	                             "from the file")
310	    parser.add_argument("--output-delimiter", choices=sorted(DELIMITERS),
311	                        default=None,
312	                        metavar="NAME",
313	                        help="field delimiter for the exported file "
314	                             "only: comma, semicolon or tab (one real "
315	                             "tab character); the input is still read "
316	                             "with --delimiter, so any combination is "
317	                             "allowed; omitting it writes with the same "
318	                             "delimiter the input was read with")
319	    parser.add_argument("--include-changes", action="store_true",
320	                        help="add a changes array to the success summary "
321	                             "with one {record, column, before, after} "
322	                             "entry per changed cell, in record order")
323	    parser.add_argument("--include-null-matches", action="store_true",
324	                        help="add a null_matches array to the success "
325	                             "summary with one {record, column, before} "
326	                             "entry per cell the normalize-null rule "
327	                             "matches, in record order, whether or not "
328	                             "the replacement changes the cell text; "
329	                             "only valid with --rule normalize-null")
330	    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
331	                        help="preview only: fully read and validate the "
332	                             "input and print the same summary JSON, but "
333	                             "create no output file or directory")
334	    return parser.parse_args(argv)
335	
336	
337	def read_records(path, delimiter):
338	    """Read all CSV records, returning a list of (record_number, fields).
339	
340	    Record numbers start at 1 for the header; quoted newlines inside a
341	    field do not advance the number. The given delimiter is used
342	    exactly as provided and is never sniffed.
343	    """
344	    records = []
345	    try:
346	        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as infile:
347	            reader = csv.reader(infile, delimiter=delimiter, strict=True)
348	            try:
349	                for record_no, record in enumerate(reader, start=1):
350	                    records.append((record_no, record))
351	            except csv.Error as exc:
352	                fail(f"cannot parse CSV in {path!r}: {exc}")
353	            except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
354	                fail(f"input file {path!r} is not valid UTF-8: {exc}")
355	    except OSError as exc:
356	        fail(f"cannot read input file {path!r}: {exc}")
357	    return records
358	
359	
360	def main(argv=None):
361	    args = parse_args(argv)
362	
363	    # argparse --delimiter choices already reject a missing value or
364	    # anything other than the lowercase names comma / semicolon / tab
365	    # (exit 2); the mapping gives the actual one-character delimiter
366	    # used for reading, with comma as the default.
367	    delimiter = DELIMITERS[args.delimiter]
368	
369	    # --output-delimiter is validated by argparse the same way. When
370	    # given it overrides only the export format; when omitted the output
371	    # reuses the input delimiter (comma by default). A format change by
372	    # itself never counts as a changed cell.
373	    output_delimiter = (
374	        DELIMITERS[args.output_delimiter]
375	        if args.output_delimiter is not None
376	        else delimiter
377	    )
378	
379	    rule = RULES.get(args.rule)
380	    if rule is None:
381	        fail(f"unsupported rule {args.rule!r} "
382	             f"(supported: {', '.join(sorted(RULES))})")
383	
384	    # --null-marker is only meaningful for normalize-null, and every
385	    # marker must name a non-empty value after str.strip() (whitespace
386	    # around the marker is tolerated; whitespace-only markers are not).
387	    if args.null_marker and args.rule != "normalize-null":
388	        fail("--null-marker can only be used with --rule normalize-null")
389	    extra_markers = set()
390	    for marker in args.null_marker:
391	        stripped_marker = marker.strip()
392	        if not stripped_marker:
393	            fail("--null-marker requires a value that is non-empty "
394	                 "after stripping surrounding whitespace")
395	        extra_markers.add(ascii_lower(stripped_marker))
396	
397	    # --null-replacement is only meaningful for normalize-null. argparse
398	    # already rejects a missing value (exit 2); any text is otherwise
399	    # accepted verbatim, including empty and whitespace-only strings.
400	    if args.null_replacement is not None and args.rule != "normalize-null":
401	        fail("--null-replacement can only be used with "
402	             "--rule normalize-null")
403	    if args.rule == "normalize-null":
404	        rule = partial(normalize_null, extra_markers=extra_markers,
405	                       replacement=args.null_replacement or "")
406

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Local CSV cleaner: apply one explicit rule to one column of a UTF-8 CSV.

Usage:
    python csv_cleaner.py --input input.csv --output cleaned.csv \
        --column name --rule trim

normalize-null additionally accepts repeatable custom null markers:

    python csv_cleaner.py --input input.csv --output cleaned.csv \
        --column name --rule normalize-null \
        --null-marker MISSING --null-marker 待补

normalize-null also accepts --null-replacement TEXT to substitute the
given text for every cell the rule would otherwise turn into an empty
string:

    python csv_cleaner.py --input input.csv --output cleaned.csv \
        --column name --rule normalize-null --null-replacement 未知

The replacement is written verbatim: it is not stripped, not
case-folded and never re-matched against the null markers, and an
empty or whitespace-only replacement is allowed. Omitting the option
keeps the default empty-string behavior. Cells whose value does not
match a marker are kept byte-for-byte either way, and a cell only
counts as changed when the replacement differs from its original
value.

The field delimiter is chosen explicitly with --delimiter:

    python csv_cleaner.py --input sample.csv --output cleaned.csv \
        --column name --rule trim --delimiter semicolon

    --delimiter accepts only the lowercase names comma, semicolon and
    tab, meaning a comma, a semicolon and one real tab character
    respectively; omitting it is the same as comma. The chosen
    delimiter is used both to read the input and to write the result,
    never guessed from the file contents.

    The export delimiter can be chosen independently with
    --output-delimiter:

    python csv_cleaner.py --input sample.csv --output cleaned.csv \
        --column name --rule trim --delimiter semicolon \
        --output-delimiter comma

    --output-delimiter accepts the same lowercase names comma,
    semicolon and tab. When given it overrides only the output format:
    the input is still read with --delimiter, and any of the three
    combinations is allowed. Omitting it keeps one shared delimiter for
    reading and writing (comma when --delimiter is also omitted). A
    change of delimiter is only a format change and never counts as a
    changed cell.

normalize-date additionally accepts --date-order to choose how a slash
date with the year last is read:

    python csv_cleaner.py --input input.csv --output cleaned.csv \
        --column due_date --rule normalize-date --date-order mdy

    --date-order accepts only lowercase dmy and mdy; omitting it is the
    same as dmy (DD/MM/YYYY). Under mdy the year-last slash date is read
    as MM/DD/YYYY, with ambiguous fields settled by the chosen order and
    no guessing or fallback. YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY/MM/DD and YYYY.MM.DD stay
    year-month-day under either order.

normalize-whitespace strips both ends and collapses every internal run
of whitespace (judged by str.isspace) to one ASCII space:

    python csv_cleaner.py --input input.csv --output cleaned.csv \
        --column name --rule normalize-whitespace

On success prints a single JSON object to stdout, e.g.
    {"rows": 3, "changed_cells": 2}
and exits 0. Any failure exits 2 with the reason on stderr and no output
file is created.

With --include-changes the same JSON object gains a "changes" array with
one {"record", "column", "before", "after"} entry per changed cell, in
record order; no separate detail file is written.

With --include-null-matches (normalize-null only) the summary also gains
a "null_matches" array with one {"record", "column", "before"} entry per
cell the null rule matches, in record order, whether or not the
replacement actually changes the cell text; the exported CSV is
unaffected and no separate detail file is written. The two detail
switches are independent and may be used together.

With --dry-run the input is fully read and validated and the same summary
JSON is printed, but no output file or directory is created. The output
path must still differ from the input and must not already exist; a
missing parent directory or unwritable location does not fail the
preview, so a successful dry run does not guarantee a real export would
succeed.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import json
import os
import re
import sys
from datetime import date
from functools import partial

NULL_MARKERS = frozenset({"null", "n/a"})

# [0-9] rather than \d so only ASCII digits are accepted.
DATE_ISO_RE = re.compile(r"^([0-9]{4})-([0-9]{2})-([0-9]{2})$")
# A slash date whose four-digit year is last. The two leading fields are
# day/month under dmy and month/day under mdy, never guessed.
DATE_SLASH_YEAR_RE = re.compile(r"^([0-9]{2})/([0-9]{2})/([0-9]{4})$")
DATE_YMD_SLASH_RE = re.compile(r"^([0-9]{4})/([0-9]{2})/([0-9]{2})$")
# A dot date is always year-month-day; the two English periods are part
# of the spelling and --date-order never applies to it.
DATE_DOT_RE = re.compile(r"^([0-9]{4})\.([0-9]{2})\.([0-9]{2})$")

# Accepted --date-order values: how to read a NN/NN/YYYY slash date.
DATE_ORDERS = ("dmy", "mdy")
DEFAULT_DATE_ORDER = "dmy"

# Accepted --delimiter / --output-delimiter names mapped to the actual
# one-character field delimiters. Each is always explicit: the input
# delimiter defaults to comma, and the output delimiter defaults to the
# input one; neither is ever sniffed.
DELIMITERS = {"comma": ",", "semicolon": ";", "tab": "\t"}
DEFAULT_DELIMITER_NAME = "comma"


class InvalidDateError(ValueError):
    """Raised when a cell is not an accepted calendar date."""


def ascii_lower(text):
    """Lowercase ASCII A-Z only; all other characters stay untouched."""
    return "".join(
        chr(ord(ch) + 32) if "A" <= ch <= "Z" else ch for ch in text
    )


def is_null_match(value, extra_markers=frozenset()):
    """Return True when the null rule would replace the cell.

    After stripping both ends, the cell matches when the result is empty
    or equals NULL / N/A (or any of the given extra markers)
    case-insensitively with respect to ASCII letters. Anything else
    (e.g. "NULLABLE") does not match.
    """
    stripped = value.strip()
    if not stripped:
        return True
    lowered = ascii_lower(stripped)
    return lowered in NULL_MARKERS or lowered in extra_markers


def normalize_null(value, extra_markers=frozenset(), replacement=""):
    """Normalize null markers to the replacement text (empty by default).

    After stripping both ends, the cell is replaced when the result is
    empty or matches NULL / N/A (or any of the given extra markers)
    case-insensitively with respect to ASCII letters. Anything else is
    returned byte-for-byte, including its surrounding whitespace (e.g.
    "NULLABLE" is not a marker). Extra markers are compared after
    str.strip() themselves; duplicate markers collapse into one match but
    never inflate the change count. The replacement is used verbatim: it
    is not stripped, not case-folded and never re-matched against the
    markers, and an empty or whitespace-only replacement is allowed.
    """
    if is_null_match(value, extra_markers):
        return replacement
    return value


# Accepted spellings that are always read year-month-day; the separator
# is part of the spelling and the three are never mixed within a value.
DATE_YMD_PATTERNS = (DATE_ISO_RE, DATE_YMD_SLASH_RE, DATE_DOT_RE)


def parse_date_fields(stripped, date_order):
    """Split an accepted date spelling into (year, month, day) ints.

    The three YYYY-first spellings always read year-month-day regardless
    of date_order. The year-last slash spelling NN/NN/YYYY follows the
    explicit order only: "dmy" reads it DD/MM/YYYY and "mdy" reads it
    MM/DD/YYYY, with no guessing or fallback. Returns None when stripped
    matches none of the accepted spellings.
    """
    for pattern in DATE_YMD_PATTERNS:
        match = pattern.match(stripped)
        if match:
            return tuple(int(part) for part in match.groups())
    match = DATE_SLASH_YEAR_RE.match(stripped)
    if match:
        first, second, year = (int(part) for part in match.groups())
        if date_order == "mdy":
            return year, first, second
        return year, second, first
    return None


def normalize_date(value, date_order=DEFAULT_DATE_ORDER):
    """Normalize an accepted date spelling to YYYY-MM-DD.

    After stripping both ends, an empty cell stays empty. Anything else
    must be exactly YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY/MM/DD, YYYY.MM.DD or a slash date
    with the four-digit year last (NN/NN/YYYY), using ASCII digits, a
    four-digit year and two-digit month/day, and must be a real
    proleptic Gregorian calendar date in years 0001-9999; the result is
    always spelled YYYY-MM-DD.

    YYYY.MM.DD is always read year-month-day with two English periods;
    like YYYY-MM-DD and YYYY/MM/DD it is unaffected by date_order. The
    year-last slash date is read by the explicit date_order only:
    "dmy" reads it as DD/MM/YYYY and "mdy" as MM/DD/YYYY. Ambiguous
    values follow that order with no guessing or fallback (under mdy
    13/02/2024 means month 13 and is invalid). YYYY-MM-DD,
    YYYY/MM/DD and YYYY.MM.DD are always year-month-day under either
    order. Internal whitespace, unpadded numbers, mixed separators,
    time suffixes and null markers such as NULL or N/A are invalid and
    raise InvalidDateError.
    """
    stripped = value.strip()
    if not stripped:
        return ""
    fields = parse_date_fields(stripped, date_order)
    if fields is None:
        raise InvalidDateError(f"invalid date: {value!r}")
    year, month, day = fields
    try:
        normalized = date(year, month, day)
    except ValueError:
        raise InvalidDateError(f"invalid date: {value!r}") from None
    return normalized.isoformat()


def normalize_whitespace(value):
    """Collapse whitespace to single ASCII spaces and strip both ends.

    Whitespace is judged by str.isspace (space, tab, carriage return,
    newline, ideographic space U+3000, ...): both ends are stripped and
    every internal run of whitespace becomes one ASCII space. An empty
    string stays empty and a whitespace-only string becomes empty. All
    other characters and their order are preserved, including the
    zero-width space U+200B, which str.isspace does not count as
    whitespace. NULL / N/A text and date text are only
    whitespace-normalized, never otherwise converted.
    """
    return " ".join(value.split())


RULES = {
    "trim": str.strip,
    "normalize-null": normalize_null,
    "normalize-date": normalize_date,
    "normalize-whitespace": normalize_whitespace,
}


def fail(message):
    print(f"error: {message}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)


def parse_args(argv):
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="csv_cleaner.py",
        description="Apply one explicit cleaning rule to one column of a "
                    "UTF-8 CSV file and write the result to a new file.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--input", required=True,
                        help="path to the input CSV file (opened read-only)")
    parser.add_argument("--output", required=True,
                        help="path to the output CSV file (must not exist yet)")
    parser.add_argument("--column", required=True,
                        help="exact name of the single column to clean")
    parser.add_argument("--rule", required=True,
                        help="cleaning rule to apply (supported: "
                             + ", ".join(sorted(RULES)) + ")")
    parser.add_argument("--null-marker", action="append", default=[],
                        metavar="MARKER",
                        help="additional whole-value null marker for "
                             "normalize-null (may be repeated; the value "
                             "is stripped at both ends and compared "
                             "case-insensitively on ASCII letters only)")
    parser.add_argument("--null-replacement", default=None,
                        metavar="TEXT",
                        help="replacement text for normalize-null: every "
                             "cell the rule would turn into an empty "
                             "string is written as TEXT instead, verbatim "
                             "(not stripped, not case-folded, never "
                             "re-matched; empty and whitespace-only text "
                             "is allowed); omitting it keeps the default "
                             "empty-string behavior")
    parser.add_argument("--date-order", choices=DATE_ORDERS, default=None,
                        metavar="ORDER",
                        help="how to read a slash date with the year last "
                             "for normalize-date: dmy (DD/MM/YYYY, the "
                             "default when omitted) or mdy (MM/DD/YYYY); "
                             "YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY/MM/DD and YYYY.MM.DD stay "
                             "year-month-day under either order")
    parser.add_argument("--delimiter", choices=sorted(DELIMITERS),
                        default=DEFAULT_DELIMITER_NAME,
                        metavar="NAME",
                        help="field delimiter for reading the input "
                             "(and for writing unless --output-delimiter "
                             "is given): comma (the default when "
                             "omitted), semicolon or tab (one real tab "
                             "character); the delimiter is never guessed "
                             "from the file")
    parser.add_argument("--output-delimiter", choices=sorted(DELIMITERS),
                        default=None,
                        metavar="NAME",
                        help="field delimiter for the exported file "
                             "only: comma, semicolon or tab (one real "
                             "tab character); the input is still read "
                             "with --delimiter, so any combination is "
                             "allowed; omitting it writes with the same "
                             "delimiter the input was read with")
    parser.add_argument("--include-changes", action="store_true",
                        help="add a changes array to the success summary "
                             "with one {record, column, before, after} "
                             "entry per changed cell, in record order")
    parser.add_argument("--include-null-matches", action="store_true",
                        help="add a null_matches array to the success "
                             "summary with one {record, column, before} "
                             "entry per cell the normalize-null rule "
                             "matches, in record order, whether or not "
                             "the replacement changes the cell text; "
                             "only valid with --rule normalize-null")
    parser.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true",
                        help="preview only: fully read and validate the "
                             "input and print the same summary JSON, but "
                             "create no output file or directory")
    return parser.parse_args(argv)


def read_records(path, delimiter):
    """Read all CSV records, returning a list of (record_number, fields).

    Record numbers start at 1 for the header; quoted newlines inside a
    field do not advance the number. The given delimiter is used
    exactly as provided and is never sniffed.
    """
    records = []
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as infile:
            reader = csv.reader(infile, delimiter=delimiter, strict=True)
            try:
                for record_no, record in enumerate(reader, start=1):
                    records.append((record_no, record))
            except csv.Error as exc:
                fail(f"cannot parse CSV in {path!r}: {exc}")
            except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
                fail(f"input file {path!r} is not valid UTF-8: {exc}")
    except OSError as exc:
        fail(f"cannot read input file {path!r}: {exc}")
    return records


def main(argv=None):
    args = parse_args(argv)

    # argparse --delimiter choices already reject a missing value or
    # anything other than the lowercase names comma / semicolon / tab
    # (exit 2); the mapping gives the actual one-character delimiter
    # used for reading, with comma as the default.
    delimiter = DELIMITERS[args.delimiter]

    # --output-delimiter is validated by argparse the same way. When
    # given it overrides only the export format; when omitted the output
    # reuses the input delimiter (comma by default). A format change by
    # itself never counts as a changed cell.
    output_delimiter = (
        DELIMITERS[args.output_delimiter]
        if args.output_delimiter is not None
        else delimiter
    )

    rule = RULES.get(args.rule)
    if rule is None:
        fail(f"unsupported rule {args.rule!r} "
             f"(supported: {', '.join(sorted(RULES))})")

    # --null-marker is only meaningful for normalize-null, and every
    # marker must name a non-empty value after str.strip() (whitespace
    # around the marker is tolerated; whitespace-only markers are not).
    if args.null_marker and args.rule != "normalize-null":
        fail("--null-marker can only be used with --rule normalize-null")
    extra_markers = set()
    for marker in args.null_marker:
        stripped_marker = marker.strip()
        if not stripped_marker:
            fail("--null-marker requires a value that is non-empty "
                 "after stripping surrounding whitespace")
        extra_markers.add(ascii_lower(stripped_marker))

    # --null-replacement is only meaningful for normalize-null. argparse
    # already rejects a missing value (exit 2); any text is otherwise
    # accepted verbatim, including empty and whitespace-only strings.
    if args.null_replacement is not None and args.rule != "normalize-null":
        fail("--null-replacement can only be used with "
             "--rule normalize-null")
    if args.rule == "normalize-null":
        rule = partial(normalize_null, extra_markers=extra_markers,
                       replacement=args.null_replacement or "")

    # --include-null-matches only reports on normalize-null matches; with
    # any other rule it is rejected before the input is even read.
    if args.include_null_matches and args.rule != "normalize-null":
        fail("--include-null-matches can only be used with "
             "--rule normalize-null")

    # --date-order only governs normalize-date. argparse already rejects
    # a missing value or anything other than the lowercase choices dmy /
    # mdy (exit 2); an explicit order paired with another rule is rejected
    # here, while omitting the option leaves every rule on its default.
    if args.date_order is not None and args.rule != "normalize-date":
        fail("--date-order can only be used with --rule normalize-date")
    date_order = args.date_order or DEFAULT_DATE_ORDER
    if args.rule == "normalize-date":
        rule = partial(normalize_date, date_order=date_order)

    if os.path.abspath(args.input) == os.path.abspath(args.output):
        fail("output path must be different from the input path")
    if os.path.exists(args.output):
        fail(f"output file already exists: {args.output!r}")

    records = read_records(args.input, delimiter)

    if not records or not records[0][1]:
        fail("input is empty: no header record")
    header = records[0][1]
    if any(name == "" for name in header):
        fail("header contains an empty column name")
    if len(set(header)) != len(header):
        fail("header contains duplicate column names")
    if args.column not in header:
        fail(f"column not found in header: {args.column!r}")
    column_index = header.index(args.column)

    expected_fields = len(header)
    out_rows = [header]
    data_rows = 0
    changed_cells = 0
    changes = []
    null_matches = []
    for record_no, record in records[1:]:
        if len(record) != expected_fields:
            fail(f"record {record_no} has {len(record)} field(s), "
                 f"expected {expected_fields}")
        record = list(record)
        original = record[column_index]
        # A null match is recorded against the original parsed text even
        # when the replacement leaves the cell byte-for-byte identical
        # (e.g. an empty cell with the default empty replacement, or a
        # marker spelled exactly like --null-replacement); the
        # replacement result itself is never re-matched.
        if args.include_null_matches and is_null_match(original,
                                                       extra_markers):
            null_matches.append({
                "record": record_no,
                "column": args.column,
                "before": original,
            })
        try:
            cleaned = rule(original)
        except InvalidDateError:
            fail(f"invalid date in column {args.column!r} "
                 f"at record {record_no}: {original!r}")
        if cleaned != original:
            changes.append({
                "record": record_no,
                "column": args.column,
                "before": original,
                "after": cleaned,
            })
            record[column_index] = cleaned
            changed_cells += 1
        out_rows.append(record)
        data_rows += 1

    if not args.dry_run:
        try:
            with open(args.output, "x", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as outfile:
                csv.writer(outfile,
                           delimiter=output_delimiter).writerows(out_rows)
        except FileExistsError:
            fail(f"output file already exists: {args.output!r}")
        except OSError as exc:
            try:
                os.unlink(args.output)
            except OSError:
                pass
            fail(f"cannot write output file {args.output!r}: {exc}")

    summary = {"rows": data_rows, "changed_cells": changed_cells}
    if args.include_null_matches:
        summary["null_matches"] = null_matches
    if args.include_changes:
        summary["changes"] = changes
    print(json.dumps(summary))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

  感）而命中；缺失 命中自定义标记 --null-marker 缺失；N/A 命中内置标
  记 n/a。before 保留解析后的原文（含两端空格），不做任何规范化。
* changes 只含记录 2 至 5 共 4 条，after 均为 N/A。记录 6 的原值 N/A
  与替代文本 N/A 相同，第 470 行比较为假，所以只命中、不变化——这正是
  两个明细相差一条的原因。
* 记录 7 的 " NULLABLE " 去两端空白后是 NULLABLE，不等于任何标记，不
  命中、不变化，原值（含两端空格）原样保留。
* 预览不创建文件或目录：第 482 行 `if not args.dry_run:` 之内的写出整块
  被跳过，运行后 missing 目录仍不存在，preview.csv 未创建，nulls.csv
  字节不变。缺失父目录本就不阻止 --dry-run（路径检查只有第 423-426 行
  的“不能与输入同路径、输出不能已存在”两项，不触碰目标文件系统位
  置）。

四、导出：写出当前目录的新文件 cleaned.csv
--------------------------------------------

去掉 --dry-run，输出改为当前目录（已存在）下尚不存在的 cleaned.csv：

    python csv_cleaner.py --input nulls.csv --output cleaned.csv --column state --rule normalize-null --null-marker 缺失 --null-replacement N/A --include-null-matches --include-changes

（见第三节）。cleaned.csv 被创建，其完整文本如下（每条记录的行尾实际为
CR+LF，这是 csv.writer 的默认行终止符；记录 2 备注引号内的换行是字段内
容，保持为单个 LF；文件为无 BOM 的 UTF-8）：

    state,note
    N/A,"line one
    line two"
    N/A,ok
    N/A,ok
    N/A,ok
    N/A,ok
     NULLABLE ,ok

核对要点：

* 表头、记录顺序和全部备注保持不变：记录 2 备注解析值仍含 line one 与
  line two 之间的真实换行，写出时由 csv.writer 自动加双引号保护；其余备
  注均为 ok。state 列记录 2 至 5 被替换为 N/A，记录 6 本就是 N/A，记录
  7 的 " NULLABLE " 连两端空格一起原样保留（空格不触发引号）。
* 文件以 "x" 模式新建（第 484 行，encoding="utf-8"、newline=""），无
  BOM；输入以只读方式打开（第 346 行 encoding="utf-8-sig"），导出后
  nulls.csv 字节不变。
* 明细开关与导出内容无关：去掉两个 --include-* 开关再导出，cleaned.csv
  完全相同，只是摘要 JSON 少了对应的键。

五、仅含表头的输入
------------------

把样例换成只有一行表头 state,note 的文件，执行第三节或第四节的命令：退
出码 0，标准错误为空，标准输出为

    {"rows": 0, "changed_cells": 0, "null_matches": [], "changes": []}

即计数为零，开启的明细键存在、数组为空；省略某个开关则对应键不出现（第
497-500 行）。导出模式下输出文件只含表头一行。

六、失败示例：三种错误预览与导出同口径拒绝
--------------------------------------------

以下三种情况无论是否加 --dry-run，行为都相同：退出码 2，标准输出为空，
标准错误报告对应原因，不创建输出文件，输入与已存在的文件内容均不变。

* --include-null-matches 配合其他规则。该开关只报告 normalize-null 的命
  中，与其他规则组合时在读取输入之前即被拒（第 409-411 行）：

      python csv_cleaner.py --input nulls.csv --output missing/preview.csv --column state --rule trim --include-null-matches --dry-run

  标准错误：

      error: --include-null-matches can only be used with --rule normalize-null

* 输出文件已存在（先成功导出过 cleaned.csv，再以其为输出）：

      python csv_cleaner.py --input nulls.csv --output cleaned.csv --column state --rule normalize-null --null-marker 缺失 --null-replacement N/A --dry-run

  标准错误（第 425-426 行；真实导出另有第 487-488 行 FileExistsError 兜
  底，口径相同）：

      error: output file already exists: 'cleaned.csv'

  已存在的 cleaned.csv 内容保持不变。

* 输出与输入同路径（abspath 相同，第 423-424 行）：

      python csv_cleaner.py --input nulls.csv --output nulls.csv --column state --rule normalize-null --null-marker 缺失 --null-replacement N/A

  标准错误：

      error: output path must be different from the input path

  输入 nulls.csv 保持不变。

七、验收提示
------------

* 以解析后的结果核对：用 CSV 解析器读 cleaned.csv（注意引号内的真实换
  行属于记录 2 的备注），用 JSON 解析器读标准输出后再比较记录号、
  before、after；标准输出里 缺失 的转义写法 \u7f3a\u5931 与字面 缺失 解
  析后相等。
* 本文所述语义均可从所标源码位置确认：匹配判定 is_null_match()（第
  141-153 行）与 ascii_lower()（第 134-138 行）、内置标记 NULL_MARKERS
  （第 106 行）、自定义标记的归一化（第 387-395 行）、替代文本原样使用
  的 normalize_null()（第 156-171 行）、命中记录的第 458-464 行、变化
  判定的第 470-478 行、写出分支第 482-494 行、摘要组装的第 496-501 行、
  路径与开关校验的第 409-411 行与第 423-426 行。

要点：分号是字段分隔符；第 2 条备注 x;y,z 同时含分号和逗号，整体被双
引号保护；第 4 条备注 `say "hi"` 中的双引号在 CSV 中写成一对双引号；
第 2、4 条的 name 分别是首尾带空格的 " Alice " 与三个空格 "   "。

三、预览：--dry-run 到缺失的 missing/preview.csv
-------------------------------------------------

约定项目根目录下不存在 missing 目录。从项目根目录执行：

    python csv_cleaner.py --input sample.csv --output missing/preview.csv --column name --rule trim --delimiter semicolon --output-delimiter comma --include-changes --dry-run

结果：退出码 0，标准错误为空，标准输出只有一个 JSON 对象：

    {"rows": 3, "changed_cells": 2, "changes": [{"record": 2, "column": "name", "before": " Alice ", "after": "Alice"}, {"record": 4, "column": "name", "before": "   ", "after": ""}]}

要点：

* rows 为 3（不含表头，记录序号从表头记为 1 开始，见 read_records()
  第 324 行的 enumerate(start=1)），changed_cells 为 2。
* changes 按记录顺序只包含记录 2 和记录 4，column 均为 "name"；
  before 保留原字符串，分别是 " Alice " 与三个空格 "   "；after 分别为
  "Alice" 与空字符串。trim 即 str.strip（RULES，第 233-238 行，trim 项
  在第 234 行）。记录 3 的 name "Bob" 去除两端空白后不变，不计入；
  note 列自始至终不被处理。
* 预览不创建文件或目录：第 437 行的写出整块被跳过，运行后 missing
  目录仍不存在，preview.csv 未创建，sample.csv 字节不变。缺失父目录
  本就不阻止 --dry-run（路径检查只在第 392-395 行做“不能与输入同路径、
  输出不能已存在”两项，不触碰目标文件系统位置）。

四、导出：写出当前目录的新文件 cleaned.csv
-------------------------------------------

去掉 --dry-run，输出改为当前目录尚不存在的 cleaned.csv：

    python csv_cleaner.py --input sample.csv --output cleaned.csv --column name --rule trim --delimiter semicolon --output-delimiter comma --include-changes

结果：退出码 0，标准错误为空，标准输出与预览完全相同的一个 JSON 对象：

    {"rows": 3, "changed_cells": 2, "changes": [{"record": 2, "column": "name", "before": " Alice ", "after": "Alice"}, {"record": 4, "column": "name", "before": "   ", "after": ""}]}

cleaned.csv 的完整文本如下（每行行尾实际为 CR+LF，这是 csv.writer 的
默认行终止符；文件为无 BOM 的 UTF-8）：

    name,note
    Alice,"x;y,z"
    Bob,ok
    ,"say ""hi"""

核对要点：

* 分隔符已整体换成逗号：表头 name,note；记录 4 的 name 清空后表现为
  行首紧跟逗号的空字段。changed_cells 仍为 2，与重分隔、重引号无关。
* 备注里的分号、逗号、双引号全部保留：第 2 条备注解析值仍是 x;y,z，
  因为含逗号，写出时由 csv.writer 自动加双引号变成 "x;y,z"（分号在
  逗号格式下已不是分隔符，但逗号要求引号，里面的分号原样保留）；
  第 4 条备注解析值仍是 say "hi"，写出时内部双引号 doubling 为
  "say ""hi"""。这些引号由写出器按逗号格式添加，不是内容变化。
* cleaned.csv 为无 BOM 的 UTF-8（第 439 行 encoding="utf-8"，不会写
  BOM）；sample.csv 以只读方式打开，导出后字节不变。

五、输出分隔符的取值边界
-------------------------

* --output-delimiter 只接受小写的 comma、semicolon、tab（第 292-300 行
  的 choices=sorted(DELIMITERS)）。省略该参数时输出沿用输入分隔符
  （第 348-352 行）；--delimiter 同时省略则读写都用逗号。

  为空、无输出文件生成（即使输入只有表头也一样）。用仅含表头
  “name;note”的文件分别演示，三条命令的标准错误均先打印一段 usage
  提示，最后一行为：

  * 缺值（--output-delimiter 后无值，例如位于命令末尾）：

        csv_cleaner.py: error: argument --output-delimiter: expected one argument

  * 空值（--output-delimiter ""）：

        csv_cleaner.py: error: argument --output-delimiter: invalid choice: '' (choose from comma, semicolon, tab)

  * 大写 Comma：

        csv_cleaner.py: error: argument --output-delimiter: invalid choice: 'Comma' (choose from comma, semicolon, tab)

  这些报错由 argparse 在 parse_args()（第 246 行起）内直接产生，程序
  在任何路径检查与写出之前即退出，因此不会创建输出文件。

六、路径边界：预览与导出同口径拒绝什么、差别在哪
--------------------------------------------------

input.content:
trim 流程的记录定位说明：空行、空字段与引号内换行（csv_cleaner.py）
=====================================================================

本文依据仓库根目录当前版本的 csv_cleaner.py，专门解释 --rule trim 一条
线上“报错里的 record 指向哪条记录”：CSV 怎样被解析成记录、记录序号如何
编号、列数校验在哪一步发生、单元格何时被 trim、结果何时写出，以及空行、
空字段、引号内换行如何影响定位。结论先行：错误信息和 changes 里的
record 是 CSV 记录序号（表头记为 1），不是文本编辑器里的物理行号；引号
内换行会占用物理行但不增加记录，引号外的空行则是一条独立记录。文中行号
对应 csv_cleaner.py 当前源码。本次只新增本文这一份说明，程序、命令行参
数、摘要 JSON 结构与既有文档均未改动。

一、一条记录是怎样编号的：read_records() 与 enumerate(start=1)
----------------------------------------------------------------

* 读取只发生在 read_records()（第 337-357 行）。第 346 行以
  encoding="utf-8-sig"、newline="" 只读打开输入（容忍一个 UTF-8 BOM，
  且不修改输入），第 347 行用
  `csv.reader(infile, delimiter=delimiter, strict=True)` 按显式分隔符
  解析——分隔符来自 --delimiter（默认逗号，见第 126-127 行与第 367
  行），从不根据文件内容猜测；strict=True 意味着引号不成对等 CSV 语法
  错误会抛 csv.Error，由第 351-352 行捕获并经 fail() 以退出码 2 失败
  （UTF-8 解码失败与读取失败分别在第 353-354、355-356 行处理）。
* 记录序号在第 349 行
  `for record_no, record in enumerate(reader, start=1)` 从 1 开始计
  数。函数文档字符串（第 338-343 行）写明：表头是第 1 条记录；引号内
  换行不推进这个序号。read_records() 返回的是
  (record_number, fields) 元组列表，此后所有环节都只用这个
  record_number，再也接触不到物理行号。
* 所以“物理行”和“记录”是两层东西：字段被双引号包住后，里面的真实
  换行只是该字段的字符，csv.reader 要读到闭合引号之后的记录结束符才
  结束这条记录——一条记录可以横跨多个物理行，record_no 却只加一次。
  反过来，引号外的换行结束当前记录；文件末尾那个正常换行只是最后一条
  记录的结束符，不会再产生一条空记录（见第八节边界一）。

二、从解析、列数校验、单元格清理到输出的先后顺序
--------------------------------------------------

main()（第 360-505 行）的顺序决定了哪类错误先报、摘要要到什么时候才可
能打印：

1. 参数与规则（第 361-421 行）。trim 在 RULES 中直接绑定为 str.strip
   （第 251-256 行，trim 项在第 252 行），不含任何额外包装；--rule 取
   值不支持在第 379-382 行拒绝。
2. 输出路径两项检查（第 423-426 行）：不能与输入指向同一路径（第
   423-424 行）、输出路径不能已存在（第 425-426 行）。--dry-run 并不
   豁免这两项。
3. 读入全部记录（第 428 行调用 read_records）。
4. 表头校验（第 430-439 行）：没有记录或第一条记录没有字段，在第
   430-431 行报 `input is empty: no header record`；表头含空列名
   （第 433-434 行）、表头重名（第 435-436 行）、找不到目标列（第
   437-438 行）各有专属报错；目标列下标 column_index 在第 439 行确
   定。
5. 逐条数据循环（第 447-480 行）。expected_fields 取表头列数（第 441
   行）。每条记录先在第 448-450 行做列数校验，不符立即
   `fail(f"record {record_no} has {len(record)} field(s), expected "
   f"{expected_fields}")` 退出 2——这一步发生在任何单元格清理之前。
   校验通过后，第 452 行只取目标列原值 original，第 466 行
   `cleaned = rule(original)`（trim 时即 str.strip）；第 470 行比较
   清洗前后，不同才在第 471-476 行追加 changes、第 477 行写回本列、
   第 478 行让 changed_cells 加一。非目标列自始至终不参与。
6. 写出结果（第 482-494 行）：仅当不是 --dry-run。第 484 行用 "x"
   独占新建模式打开输出（encoding="utf-8"、newline=""，无 BOM），第
   485-486 行 `csv.writer(outfile, delimiter=output_delimiter)
   .writerows(out_rows)` 写出全部行。
7. 打印摘要（第 496-501 行）：summary 先放 rows、changed_cells（第
   496 行），加了 --include-changes（参数定义在第 319-322 行）才在第
   499-500 行附加 changes 数组，最后第 501 行 print(json.dumps
   (summary))。

关键推论：列数错误在第 449 行经 fail()（第 259-261 行：向 stderr 打印
`error: ...` 后 sys.exit(2)）直接终止，永远到不了第 501 行。所以即便
出错记录之前已经存在可清理的值，也不会得到“前半截”摘要，真实导出时
更到不了第 482 行的写出块——标准输出为空，也没有半成品文件。

三、空行、空字段、引号内换行：四种长相，四种字段数
------------------------------------------------------

csv.reader 按“分隔符切出了几个字段”计数，并不看物理行是否空白：

* 引号外空行（且不是文件末尾那个结束换行）：切不出任何字段，是一条 0
  字段记录（本文第七节的 record 5 即属此类）。
* 独立的纯空格行：空格是未加引号字段里的普通字符，整行就是一个含若干
  空格的字段，即 1 字段记录；在双列表头下因列数不符退出 2。
* 单独一个逗号 `,`：分隔符在左右各切出一个字段，两个字段都是空字符
  串，即 2 字段记录，列数与表头一致，合法。空“字段”与零字段的“空
  行”是两回事：数据行允许有空字段（只有表头不允许有空列名，第 433-
  434 行）。
* 引号内换行（连同引号内的空行）：换行被双引号保护，属于该字段解析值
  的一部分，既不结束记录也不产生空记录；物理行变多、记录不增多。

四、成功样例输入 records.csv
-----------------------------

在项目根目录把以下内容原样保存为 UTF-8 编码的 records.csv（默认逗号分
隔；每个物理行末尾为一个 LF，最后一行 `"   ",` 之后也有一个正常的末尾
换行；当前目录若已有同名 records.csv，请先备份或换到空目录）。注意第
三个物理行是整行没有任何字符的空行，且它位于一对双引号之内：

    name,note
    " Alice ","line one

    line three"
    ,ok
    "   ",

物理行与 CSV 记录的对应关系如下（这正是“record 不等于编辑器行号”的
样子）：

  物理行 1  name,note                    记录 1（表头，2 字段）
  物理行 2  " Alice ","line one          记录 2 开始
  物理行 3  （整行为空，位于引号内）     仍属于记录 2 的 note 字段
  物理行 4  line three"                 记录 2 结束（note 的引号闭合）
  物理行 5  ,ok                         记录 3
  物理行 6  "   ",                      记录 4（行尾 LF 仅结束本记录）

文件有 6 个物理行，却只有 4 条记录。三条数据记录解析后的值为：

* 记录 2：name 为两端各一个 ASCII 空格的 ` Alice `；note 为
  `line one` 与 `line three` 之间夹着连续两个真实换行
  （"line one\n\nline three"），那两个 LF 一个结束物理行 2、一个构成
  空的物理行 3，但都在引号内。
* 记录 3（物理行 5，`,ok`）：name 为空字符串；note 为 `ok`。
* 记录 4（物理行 6，`"   ",`）：name 为三个 ASCII 空格；note 为空字
  符串。

五、导出命令与预期摘要
------------------------

从项目根目录执行（清理 name 列并开启 --include-changes，输出到尚不存
在的 cleaned.csv）：

    python csv_cleaner.py --input records.csv --output cleaned.csv --column name --rule trim --include-changes

结果：退出码 0，标准错误为空，标准输出只有一行 JSON 对象：

    {"rows": 3, "changed_cells": 2, "changes": [{"record": 2, "column": "name", "before": " Alice ", "after": "Alice"}, {"record": 4, "column": "name", "before": "   ", "after": ""}]}

核对要点：

* rows 为 3，即三条数据记录（不含表头）；changed_cells 为 2。
* changes 按记录顺序只含记录 2 和记录 4，column 均为 "name"。记录 2
  的 before 保留两端各一个空格（" Alice "），after 为 "Alice"；记录 4

trim 流程的记录定位说明：空行、空字段与引号内换行（csv_cleaner.py）
=====================================================================

本文依据仓库根目录当前版本的 csv_cleaner.py，专门解释 --rule trim 一条
线上“报错里的 record 指向哪条记录”：CSV 怎样被解析成记录、记录序号如何
编号、列数校验在哪一步发生、单元格何时被 trim、结果何时写出，以及空行、
空字段、引号内换行如何影响定位。结论先行：错误信息和 changes 里的
record 是 CSV 记录序号（表头记为 1），不是文本编辑器里的物理行号；引号
内换行会占用物理行但不增加记录，引号外的空行则是一条独立记录。文中行号
对应 csv_cleaner.py 当前源码。本次只新增本文这一份说明，程序、命令行参
数、摘要 JSON 结构与既有文档均未改动。

一、一条记录是怎样编号的：read_records() 与 enumerate(start=1)
----------------------------------------------------------------

* 读取只发生在 read_records()（第 337-357 行）。第 346 行以
  encoding="utf-8-sig"、newline="" 只读打开输入（容忍一个 UTF-8 BOM，
  且不修改输入），第 347 行用
  `csv.reader(infile, delimiter=delimiter, strict=True)` 按显式分隔符
  解析——分隔符来自 --delimiter（默认逗号，见第 126-127 行与第 367
  行），从不根据文件内容猜测；strict=True 意味着引号不成对等 CSV 语法
  错误会抛 csv.Error，由第 351-352 行捕获并经 fail() 以退出码 2 失败
  （UTF-8 解码失败与读取失败分别在第 353-354、355-356 行处理）。
* 记录序号在第 349 行
  `for record_no, record in enumerate(reader, start=1)` 从 1 开始计
  数。函数文档字符串（第 338-343 行）写明：表头是第 1 条记录；引号内
  换行不推进这个序号。read_records() 返回的是
  (record_number, fields) 元组列表，此后所有环节都只用这个
  record_number，再也接触不到物理行号。
* 所以“物理行”和“记录”是两层东西：字段被双引号包住后，里面的真实
  换行只是该字段的字符，csv.reader 要读到闭合引号之后的记录结束符才
  结束这条记录——一条记录可以横跨多个物理行，record_no 却只加一次。
  反过来，引号外的换行结束当前记录；文件末尾那个正常换行只是最后一条
  记录的结束符，不会再产生一条空记录（见第八节边界一）。

二、从解析、列数校验、单元格清理到输出的先后顺序
--------------------------------------------------

main()（第 360-505 行）的顺序决定了哪类错误先报、摘要要到什么时候才可
能打印：

1. 参数与规则（第 361-421 行）。trim 在 RULES 中直接绑定为 str.strip
   （第 251-256 行，trim 项在第 252 行），不含任何额外包装；--rule 取
   值不支持在第 379-382 行拒绝。
2. 输出路径两项检查（第 423-426 行）：不能与输入指向同一路径（第
   423-424 行）、输出路径不能已存在（第 425-426 行）。--dry-run 并不
   豁免这两项。
3. 读入全部记录（第 428 行调用 read_records）。
4. 表头校验（第 430-439 行）：没有记录或第一条记录没有字段，在第
   430-431 行报 `input is empty: no header record`；表头含空列名
   （第 433-434 行）、表头重名（第 435-436 行）、找不到目标列（第
   437-438 行）各有专属报错；目标列下标 column_index 在第 439 行确
   定。
5. 逐条数据循环（第 447-480 行）。expected_fields 取表头列数（第 441
   行）。每条记录先在第 448-450 行做列数校验，不符立即
   `fail(f"record {record_no} has {len(record)} field(s), expected "
   f"{expected_fields}")` 退出 2——这一步发生在任何单元格清理之前。
   校验通过后，第 452 行只取目标列原值 original，第 466 行
   `cleaned = rule(original)`（trim 时即 str.strip）；第 470 行比较
   清洗前后，不同才在第 471-476 行追加 changes、第 477 行写回本列、
   第 478 行让 changed_cells 加一。非目标列自始至终不参与。
6. 写出结果（第 482-494 行）：仅当不是 --dry-run。第 484 行用 "x"
   独占新建模式打开输出（encoding="utf-8"、newline=""，无 BOM），第
   485-486 行 `csv.writer(outfile, delimiter=output_delimiter)
   .writerows(out_rows)` 写出全部行。
7. 打印摘要（第 496-501 行）：summary 先放 rows、changed_cells（第
   496 行），加了 --include-changes（参数定义在第 319-322 行）才在第
   499-500 行附加 changes 数组，最后第 501 行 print(json.dumps
   (summary))。

关键推论：列数错误在第 449 行经 fail()（第 259-261 行：向 stderr 打印
`error: ...` 后 sys.exit(2)）直接终止，永远到不了第 501 行。所以即便
出错记录之前已经存在可清理的值，也不会得到“前半截”摘要，真实导出时
更到不了第 482 行的写出块——标准输出为空，也没有半成品文件。

三、空行、空字段、引号内换行：四种长相，四种字段数
------------------------------------------------------

csv.reader 按“分隔符切出了几个字段”计数，并不看物理行是否空白：

* 引号外空行（且不是文件末尾那个结束换行）：切不出任何字段，是一条 0
  字段记录（本文第七节的 record 5 即属此类）。
* 独立的纯空格行：空格是未加引号字段里的普通字符，整行就是一个含若干
  空格的字段，即 1 字段记录；在双列表头下因列数不符退出 2。
* 单独一个逗号 `,`：分隔符在左右各切出一个字段，两个字段都是空字符
  串，即 2 字段记录，列数与表头一致，合法。空“字段”与零字段的“空
  行”是两回事：数据行允许有空字段（只有表头不允许有空列名，第 433-
  434 行）。
* 引号内换行（连同引号内的空行）：换行被双引号保护，属于该字段解析值
  的一部分，既不结束记录也不产生空记录；物理行变多、记录不增多。

四、成功样例输入 records.csv
-----------------------------

在项目根目录把以下内容原样保存为 UTF-8 编码的 records.csv（默认逗号分
隔；每个物理行末尾为一个 LF，最后一行 `"   ",` 之后也有一个正常的末尾
换行；当前目录若已有同名 records.csv，请先备份或换到空目录）。注意第
三个物理行是整行没有任何字符的空行，且它位于一对双引号之内：

    name,note
    " Alice ","line one

    line three"
    ,ok
    "   ",

物理行与 CSV 记录的对应关系如下（这正是“record 不等于编辑器行号”的
样子）：

  物理行 1  name,note                    记录 1（表头，2 字段）
  物理行 2  " Alice ","line one          记录 2 开始
  物理行 3  （整行为空，位于引号内）     仍属于记录 2 的 note 字段
  物理行 4  line three"                 记录 2 结束（note 的引号闭合）
  物理行 5  ,ok                         记录 3
  物理行 6  "   ",                      记录 4（行尾 LF 仅结束本记录）

文件有 6 个物理行，却只有 4 条记录。三条数据记录解析后的值为：

* 记录 2：name 为两端各一个 ASCII 空格的 ` Alice `；note 为
  `line one` 与 `line three` 之间夹着连续两个真实换行
  （"line one\n\nline three"），那两个 LF 一个结束物理行 2、一个构成
  空的物理行 3，但都在引号内。
* 记录 3（物理行 5，`,ok`）：name 为空字符串；note 为 `ok`。
* 记录 4（物理行 6，`"   ",`）：name 为三个 ASCII 空格；note 为空字
  符串。

五、导出命令与预期摘要
------------------------

从项目根目录执行（清理 name 列并开启 --include-changes，输出到尚不存
在的 cleaned.csv）：

    python csv_cleaner.py --input records.csv --output cleaned.csv --column name --rule trim --include-changes

结果：退出码 0，标准错误为空，标准输出只有一行 JSON 对象：

    {"rows": 3, "changed_cells": 2, "changes": [{"record": 2, "column": "name", "before": " Alice ", "after": "Alice"}, {"record": 4, "column": "name", "before": "   ", "after": ""}]}

核对要点：

* rows 为 3，即三条数据记录（不含表头）；changed_cells 为 2。
* changes 按记录顺序只含记录 2 和记录 4，column 均为 "name"。记录 2
  的 before 保留两端各一个空格（" Alice "），after 为 "Alice"；记录 4
  的 before 保留三个 ASCII 空格（"   "），after 为空字符串。before 是
  解析后的原字符串，空白不预先规范化（第 452、471-476 行）。
* 记录 3 的 name 本就是空字符串，str.strip 后仍为空字符串，第 470 行
  比较为假，不收录；note 列从不处理。引号内那两个换行因此完全不影响
  记录序号——报错或明细中若出现记录 4，指的是物理行 6 那条数据。

六、导出文本 cleaned.csv
-------------------------

cleaned.csv 被创建，完整内容如下（记录之间的行尾实际为 CR+LF，这是
csv.writer 的默认行终止符；记录 2 备注引号内的两个换行保持为两个真实
LF，不被改写；文件为无 BOM 的 UTF-8）。其中第三物理行同样是引号内的
空行，整行无字符：

    name,note
    Alice,"line one

    line three"
    ,ok
    ,

核对要点：

* 表头仍为 name,note，记录顺序不变。记录 2 的 name 去掉两端空格后不
  再需要引号，写作 Alice；其 note 因含真实换行，写出时由 csv.writer
  自动加双引号保护，解析值仍是 line one 与 line three 之间两个真实换
  行。记录 3 仍是 `,ok`（name 空、note 为 ok）。记录 4 的 name 由三
  个空格变为空字符串，note 本就为空，整行写作单独一个逗号 `,`（两个
  有效空字段，不是 0 字段的空行）。
* 三条备注的解析内容不变：记录 2 的两个真实换行、记录 3 的 ok、记录 4
  的空字符串均与输入一致；变化只发生在 name 列。
* 输入 records.csv 以只读方式打开（第 346 行），导出后其字节保持原
  样；输出为无 BOM 的 UTF-8（第 484 行 encoding="utf-8"）。

七、失败样例：正常末尾换行之后再加一个引号外空行
---------------------------------------------------

把 records.csv 原样保留，在其末尾那个正常换行之后再追加一个空行（即再
多写一个 LF，且该空行在任何引号之外），另存为 records_bad.csv。于是文
件多出物理行 7（整行为空、引号外），它被解析成记录 5，一条 0 字段记
录；前面的记录 1-4 与成功样例完全相同，其中记录 2、4 的 name 仍然是可
清理的值。

约定项目根目录下不存在 missing 目录，执行一次 --dry-run（输出路径
missing/preview.csv 尚不存在且与输入不同）：

    python csv_cleaner.py --input records_bad.csv --output missing/preview.csv --column name --rule trim --include-changes --dry-run

结果：退出码 2，标准输出为空，标准错误恰好为下面一行：

    error: record 5 has 0 field(s), expected 2

核对要点：

* 报错中的 5 是记录序号（表头记 1，物理行 7 那条引号外空行是记录
  5），不是把引号内换行也算进行号得到的物理行号；列数校验在第 448-
  450 行、expected_fields 为表头列数 2（第 441 行）。
* 不创建任何文件或目录：运行后 missing 目录仍不存在，preview.csv 未

  更早的第 449 行。
* 不产生部分摘要：尽管记录 2、4 已有可清理的 name，第 449 行 fail()
  直接退出，第 496-501 行的摘要组装与打印不会执行，所以标准输出为空，
  而不是先给出半截 changes。records_bad.csv 字节不变。

八、边界汇总
--------------

一、正常末尾换行不增加记录。records.csv 最后一行 `"   ",` 后的那个 LF
    只是记录 4 的结束符，解析结果是 4 条记录、rows 为 3；要再出现一个
    引号外空行才会多出记录 5（第七节）。

二、引号内空行（引号内换行）属于字段。它占用物理行、出现在该字段的解
    析值里，但不推进记录序号，也不触发列数错误；闭合引号后记录才结
    束。strict=True（第 347 行）下引号必须正确配对，否则按 CSV 解析错
    误在第 351-352 行失败，那是另一类错误。

三、单独的逗号表示两个有效空字段。`,` 解析为两个空字符串，列数与双列
    表头一致，是合法数据行（实测 `name,note` 表头加一行 `,` 时预览退
    出 0，rows 为 1、changed_cells 为 0）。数据单元格允许为空；只有表
    头位置的空列名才被第 433-434 行拒绝。

四、独立的纯空格行只有一个字段。例如 `name,note` 表头、一条正常记录后
